name: Peter’s denial
charge: Denying Christ three times with cursing and swearing
summary: Peter said that though all men should be offended because of him he would never be offended, and that though he should die with him he would not deny him (Matthew 26:33-35). In the high priest’s hall he denied it to a damsel, then with an oath, and then with cursing and swearing that he did not know the man, and the cock crew (Matthew 26:69-75). The Lord turned and looked on Peter, and he remembered the word that had been spoken to him, and went out and wept bitterly (Luke 22:60-62).
offenseFull: Before the denial he was warned and he was prayed for. Satan had desired to have them, to sift them as wheat, and Christ told Peter he had prayed for him that his faith fail not, and that when he was converted he should strengthen his brethren (Luke 22:31-32). Peter had walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm: the law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul (Psalms 19:7), and that is also what he was to strengthen his brethren with. Peter answered out of his own confidence that he was ready to go both into prison and to death, and was told what he would do before the cock crew (Luke 22:33-34). A man does not know tomorrow, for his life is a vapour that appears for a little time and then vanishes away (James 4:14-15).

He denied three times. The third time he was picked out by his speech, because he was a Galilaean; the way he talked gave him away, so that he sounded like the man he was denying (Luke 22:54-60). Matthew records the oath, and then the cursing and swearing that he did not know the man (Matthew 26:69-75). The warning about that stands in the same gospel: whoever confesses him before men, him will he confess before his Father, and whoever denies him before men will be denied (Matthew 10:32-33). It was the hour given to the other side, as Christ told the chief priests and the captains of the temple when they came out against him with swords and staves, that this was their hour and the power of darkness (Luke 22:52-53). Isaiah had written it plainly of the servant: he was despised and rejected of men, and we hid as it were our faces from him, and we esteemed him not (Isaiah 53:3). That verse is Peter in the courtyard.
judgmentFull: The look and the tears are the first part of the answer. The Lord turned and looked on Peter, and Peter remembered the word and went out and wept bitterly (Luke 22:60-62). The difference between this case and the traitor in the same chapter is what came after the weeping. When Judas saw what he had done he did not go back and reconcile; he went and hanged himself (Matthew 27:3-5). Peter reconciled. Godly sorrow works repentance to salvation, but the sorrow of the world works death (2 Corinthians 7:10).

The reconciliation is recorded. After the resurrection Christ asked Peter three times whether he loved him and three times charged him to feed his lambs and his sheep, once for each denial, and Peter was grieved at the third asking (John 21:15-17). Then he was told by what death he should glorify God, that when he was old another would gird him and carry him where he would not (John 21:18-19), which answers what he had been told in the upper room, that where Christ was going he could not follow then but should follow afterwards (John 13:36). The history says he was held nine months in prison at Rome, converted the keepers and others while he was in there, and was scourged and crucified with his head downward, a position he asked for because he did not count himself worthy to die as his master died. The man who bounced back from that courtyard is the same man who stood at the gate called Beautiful and told a lame beggar that he had no silver and gold, but gave him what he had (Acts 3:1-8). The charge given with the warning stood: once converted, he was to strengthen his brethren. The fall did not cancel the man, and it did not cancel what he was sent to teach.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not lie to one another.
You shall not swear by God's name falsely.
We should avoid making any oaths so that you may not fall under judgment.
True repentance is evidenced by one's fruits.

text.text: Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended.
Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.
Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.
But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.
And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.
And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee.
Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.
And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.
And he said unto him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.
And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.
Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.
And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.
And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.
And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.
And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilean.
And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.
Then Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders, which were come to him, Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?
When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.
And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.
For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
Simon Peter said unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered him, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterwards.
Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.
And a certain man lame from his mother’s womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
Who seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple asked an alms.
And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us.
And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them.
Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.
And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.
And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.
And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:
And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.
But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilean, and thy speech agreeth thereto.
But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?
Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
